Its for two reasons. The first, and most obvious reason is that Voat is gaining so many members that the IT considerations are staggering. You start off with IT infrastructure that can support a certain amount of people, and before you're even finished implementing it the system needs to hold more people. That kind of growth is not good, its not good because its just like overheating an engine. This isn't a matter of competence at all, you simply can't afford to start a website with IT infrastructure like this, it costs a lot of money to run servers that can handle a lot of users. They have to put money in to get that technology running, but more importantly they have to find people to work on it, which is difficult. I'm assuming that voat is using cloud computing, and its really hard to find people that are sys admins for cloud based tech right now. They are in high demand, its not as trivial as posting a job ad and getting someone in working within days, its more like a couple weeks.

So, you stop the flow and make it invite only. This might seem like a horrible idea, but truly its not, its quite brilliant. The invite process makes voat seem exclusive, its the 'cool club' effect. This isn't uncommon at all and in fact Facebook started off this way. Gmail started off this way too, the Beta was invite only. Voat is in Alpha right now.

So, the decision allows voat to control the growth of the site, which is difficult and at the same time it allows them to make voat start to look exclusive and cool.
